strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Lets a headless caller explicitly authorize a small bounded continuation budget on the existing headless.continue_once method so several eligible tasks can be advanced in one replay-safe call.
Derives deterministic per-step continuation ids from a caller-provided root id and reuses HeadlessContinuationDecisionRecorded evidence for replay without duplicate task-running events.
Keeps budget admission, step replay, route boundaries, and stop reasons in Rust; VSIX only validates the bounded protocol shape.
Advances multiple currently eligible created or queued controlled tasks while still stopping at explicit recovery, apply, verifier retry, and parent-join boundaries.
Uses persisted task.list progress fingerprints and aggregate sequence between steps so callers can reason about bounded progress without client-side graph policy.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development directly, supported by persistent_structured_ledger, runtime_permission_enforcement, subtask_orchestration, and progress_visualization.
answers.new_capability: A caller can pass max_steps 1-3 to headless.continue_once and the Rust runtime will execute or replay multiple eligible continuation steps under one explicit budget, returning bounded step summaries and a stop reason.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M11.2 provides a replay-safe single step only. Headless controllers must repeatedly round-trip and reconstruct stop logic client-side to advance more than one eligible task, which weakens deterministic long-running operation.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Scheduled autonomous development remains limited to one task per caller request even when several eligible tasks are ready, forcing external callers to own continuation loops and boundary interpretation.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M11.1 introduced one authorized selected task execution; M11.2 added replay and next_route for one step; M10.2 was read-only progress aggregation. M11.3 adds bounded multi-step execution/replay using those primitives.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The existing headless.continue_once method is extended with optional max_steps; no new RPC is added.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. Budget counts and per-step summaries are execution result metadata, not a report, digest, history, verdict, readiness wrapper, or preview-only surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Rust now derives per-step continuation ids, repeatedly invokes the one-step continuation contract up to a small authorized budget, refreshes expected progress from post-step state, and stops at explicit route boundaries.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: It gives scheduled/headless callers a replay-safe bounded continuation primitive for long-running development without introducing an unbounded scheduler or VSIX-owned policy loop.
answers.milestone_progress: M11 moves from replay-safe single-step continuation to bounded caller-authorized multi-step continuation, a required vertical slice before future higher-level autonomous loop control.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M11.3 changes the deterministic current phase manifest and adds an archived M11.3 manifest. Review must confirm bounded multi-step runtime execution/replay behavior, not a wrapper or guard-only phase.

exit_criteria: headless.continue_once accepts max_steps 1-3 and rejects max_steps 0 or greater than 3
max_steps greater than 1 requires a bounded continuation_id before any ledger mutation
A budget call can execute two eligible continuation tasks sequentially through existing task.run admission
Budget execution derives deterministic per-step continuation ids from the caller root continuation_id
Repeating the same budget call replays prior per-step decisions without duplicate HeadlessContinuationDecisionRecorded or TaskRunning evidence
Budget execution stops at budget exhaustion with bounded count and stop_reason metadata
Budget execution stops at stale progress, no eligible task, task_in_progress, verification recovery, recovery proposal review, recovery apply, verification retry, and parent-join route boundaries
VSIX validates max_steps, budget counts, stop_reason, and per-step summaries without owning selection or route policy
No raw prompt, provider response, file content, ledger payload, stdout, stderr, command, environment, path, request body, secret, or arbitrary percentage is stored or returned
